statusNote: South University-Savannah Online is the IPEDS online-delivery reporting unit tied to South University's main Savannah, GA campus; it is not a separately incorporated or separately led institution. It shares governance and leadership (a single system-wide Chancellor/CEO) with South University as a whole, which is what the leadership list below reflects. South University converted from a for-profit chain (owned by the South family, then Education Management Corporation from 2003, then Dream Center Education Holdings from 2017) to an independent nonprofit university on July 14, 2023, under the Education Principle Foundation.

leaders.notes: Member of the family that owned South University; led it as President for decades (in place well before 1996) before the board named him Chancellor in October 2001. Sold the university to Education Management Corporation in 2003 while retaining the Chancellor/CEO title, and remained in that role through EDMC's 2017 sale of the university to Dream Center Education Holdings, departing in 2019.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice-Chancellor for Academic Affairs (2007-2013); originally Dean, College of Business
leaders.notes: Long-time South University administrator promoted to Chancellor and CEO on August 30, 2019, as the university transitioned toward independent nonprofit status. Replaced as CEO/Chancellor by Benjamin J. DeGweck effective November 1, 2025.

Higher-education attorney (also a former shareholder in the Higher Education Practice Group at Maynard Nexsen PC) named CEO and Chancellor effective October 31/November 1, 2025, as South University navigates financial pressure including a $35.4 million balloon debt payment and accreditation scrutiny.

Fifth president; led SEBTS through the Southern Baptist Convention's conservative resurgence, reorganizing the seminary theologically and expanding doctoral programs. Left in 2003 to lead Southwestern Baptist Theological Seminary; was later terminated by Southwestern's trustees in 2018 following mishandling of sexual-abuse-related complaints.

leaders.priorTitle: VP for Institutional Advancement / Senior Professor of Christian Education
leaders.notes: Named interim president in July 2003 (having served on the SEBTS staff since 1993) while trustees conducted a worldwide search that concluded with Daniel Akin's election in January 2004.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean, School of Theology / SVP for Academic Administration
leaders.priorInstitution: The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary, Louisville, KY
leaders.notes: Sixth president, elected unanimously January 15, 2004. One of the longest-serving presidents of any SBC seminary; announced retirement effective July 31, 2026, to be succeeded by Scott Pace.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Dean of Graduate Studies
leaders.notes: Unanimously elected seventh president by trustees on April 21, 2026; formally assumes office August 1, 2026. Previously served SEBTS as director of the Center for Preaching and Pastoral Leadership, VP of undergraduate studies/dean of Judson College, then provost; also taught nine years at Oklahoma Baptist University.

statusNote: The name of Southeastern's president for the 1996-1998 stretch (immediately before Mark Rutland's January 1999 appointment) could not be reliably identified from accessible sources in this research pass and is omitted rather than guessed; recommend revisiting in a later backfill pass with access to SEU's own institutional archives.

leaders.priorInstitution: Calvary Assembly of God, Orlando, FL
leaders.notes: Took over a financially struggling, declining-enrollment college (then Southeastern College) in January 1999; grew enrollment from roughly 1,000 to over 3,000 and led its transition to full university status with over $50 million in campus investment. Left in 2009 to become Oral Roberts University's third president (served there until 2012).

Became SEU's 15th president on February 1, 2011, after roughly a two-year gap in which the university had no permanent president following Rutland's 2009 departure (enrollment reportedly dipped during the vacancy). Enrollment subsequently grew from about 2,500 in 2011 to over 13,000 by 2025-26.

statusNote: SIUE is one of two campuses (with SIU Carbondale) of the Southern Illinois University System, overseen by a separate SIU System President (currently Daniel F. Mahony, since March 2020); the local campus head, listed below, holds the title Chancellor.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: SIUE's first woman chancellor (1994-1997). Left to become chancellor of the University of Nebraska Omaha, a post she held until resigning in 2007.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: Long-time SIUE faculty member (joined 1968) and dean of the School of Business (1975-1987) before becoming provost, then interim chancellor in 1997 and formally SIUE's sixth chancellor in 1999. After retiring in 2004, took interim leadership posts elsewhere, including interim president of Mansfield University of PA (2005-06) and interim provost of Indiana University of Pennsylvania (2007-08).

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and VP for Academic Affairs / CIO
leaders.notes: SIUE's seventh chancellor (2004-2012); oversaw the university's move to NCAA Division I athletics. Died in 2023.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice Chancellor for Academic and Student Affairs
leaders.notes: SIUE's eighth chancellor; instituted a strategic plan emphasizing online courses and international partnerships/enrollment. Resigned effective August 14, 2015, citing a desire to be closer to family.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean, Graduate School (also interim Dean, College of Arts and Sciences)
leaders.notes: Longtime SIUE history professor and graduate dean who served a one-year term as interim chancellor (Aug 15, 2015 - Jul 31, 2016) while a permanent successor to Furst-Bowe was recruited.

SIUE's ninth chancellor and an SIUE alumnus, appointed August 1, 2016. Announced his retirement in 2021, citing the unsustainable pace of the role after a difficult stretch including the COVID-19 pandemic; departed in 2022.

leaders.priorTitle: Assistant Vice Chancellor and Senior Strategist, Office of the Chancellor
leaders.notes: SIUE's tenth chancellor and the first Black chancellor in the university's history; assumed duties March 1, 2022. Previously served as deputy assistant secretary at the U.S. Department of Education, administering more than $7 billion in federal higher-education programming.
